narrative: The model estimated a 16% chance that you will fail the final year. That is a low but non-zero risk; in this review it was still enough to flag you for remedial courses as a precaution, so treat the requirement as an early-warning action rather than a certainty. The strongest signal in your record was that you have no past class failures, which counted in your favour and pushed the estimate toward passing. Your clear intention to continue into higher education was the next most influential factor and also argued against failing. Your absence count was the third most important factor; at 22 absences it is far above the passing-group average of about 4, and the model nevertheless treated this item as reducing, not increasing, the estimated failure risk in your case. Because the leading factors actually support passing, the failure flag appears to come from a weaker combination of other risks, such as weekly study time under two hours while most passing students study two to five hours or more, no school support or paid classes, and very high going-out time. To improve, use the remedial support to raise study time, attend consistently to bring absences near the passing average, and reduce competing out-of-school time; keep the strong signals—no past failures and your higher-education goal—visible in your work.
